title: Keep a selected case's source through the Show latest file read in mounted cases

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage: SEED-413#show-latest-source-file-read-cases at 07081fc48bcab56f6393afacb626fd6d1ea39ebc

Verdict: Caught.

Promise checked (Failed then retried; plan 728 key example; seed scope "preserve each distinct assertion: target line ..."): after Show latest, if the new revision's file read fails, the selected Optimization Candidates entry's source keeps its old text, line 44 targeted, revision label, offset and focus, and shows `<path> could not be read at revision <after>; showing <before>. Retry`. The caller's suggested promise, fault, command and assertion all held at this revision and were used without change.

Fault: dashboard/src/IntentFileReading.tsx line 129. The targetLine condition was changed from `text === undefined || caseTarget === undefined` to `text === undefined || caseTarget === undefined || failedRevision !== undefined`, so the target line is dropped whenever a later revision's read has failed. No fixtures or assertions were changed.

Command (scratch checkout, Node 24.21.0, after npm ci): env -u NO_COLOR -u FORCE_COLOR -u GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES caffeinate -s -i npm run --silent test:dashboard:frontend -- intent/intent-source-target-recovery-mounted

Run observations:
- Baseline (no fault): exit 0, 2/2 passed. Held then released took 921 ms, failed then retried 855 ms. Vitest Duration was 2.92s. Both cases ran on mounted Chromium.
- With the fault: exit 1. Held then released passed (915 ms), which is expected because failedRevision stays unset on that path. Failed then retried failed after 1869 ms, Vitest Duration 3.52s.
- Catching assertion: in dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-source-target-recovery-mounted.spec.ts:169, `readsLine44(source, offset, before, "assert True")` runs after `browser.failsWith(...)` and calls `source.targets(44)`. That fails at dashboard/frontend-tests/intent/intent-file-reading-page.ts:30, where `expect.poll(() => targets().length).toBe(1)` gets "expected +0 to be 1" because no `.source-line.is-target` remains. The trace shows that the earlier `failsWith` assertion passed and the failure text was present. So the run reached the failed-read path, and the catch is specifically the loss of the line 44 target.
- Separate check of the wrong behavior: I added a temporary witness spec to the scratch checkout only, then deleted it. It repeats the failed-then-retried setup up to `failsWith` and `shows("assert True")`, then logs the DOM without asserting. Without the fault it logged `targets=["44/location"] ariaCurrent=["44"] hasOldText=true`. With the fault it logged `targets=[] ariaCurrent=[] hasOldText=true`. The old text was still shown, but line 44 was no longer the targeted, aria-current location. That is a real break of the promise.

Restoration: the original file was copied out before the fault. An EXIT trap restored it after the faulted runs, and I deleted the witness spec. Afterwards `git diff --quiet` returned clean and `git status` showed no untracked source files (only the git-ignored test-results). The same command rerun after restoring: exit 0, 2/2 passed (684 ms and 764 ms), Duration 2.61s. I then removed the scratch worktree with `git worktree remove`. Evidence (logs, fault.diff, original file copy) is in /Users/terryyin/.claude/jobs/e9cbea00/tmp/coverage-evidence/. The coordinator's story worktree was not touched.

Next proof action: none needed for this promise. The maintained failed-then-retried case catches the loss of the line 44 target on the failed-read path. This matches what the SEED-300 done record's earlier coverage report said about the replaced built-app spec: the mounted replacement keeps that catch. This is a recognition of the prior result, not a new repair decision. The claim covers only the observed path (target line after a failed new-revision read). Offset, focus and the revision label were not faulted separately.

Costs:
- Test runtime (measured, Vitest "Duration" per run): baseline 2.92s, faulted 3.52s, restored 2.61s. The two witness runs were each about the same length (their Durations were not extracted). The baseline command's wall clock was 5s including npm/Vitest startup.
- Human effort: unavailable. No human took part in this check.
- Agent effort: unavailable. There is no separately supported token or time measure for this agent's work.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 95604 ms (measured), from 1795157724949 to 1795157820553 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.

## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision 07081fc48bcab56f6393afacb626fd6d1ea39ebc: Caught, no follow-up.
